report.summary: Analyzed chunk 1 of session.py: module-level docstring with design rationale, no executable code.
risks: docstring | medium | Module docstring makes many behavioral claims (e.g., no majority field, live wiring defaults to False) that cannot be verified from this chunk alone; if implementation diverges, docstring becomes misleading. | Verify each claim against the actual code in later chunks.
todos: Check that the actual class CouncilRecord has no approve/reject/score/majority/consensus/confidence field.
Verify that convene() has a live parameter defaulting to False and raises LiveCouncilRefused when live=False and adapter has a shipped transport.
Check that live_egress_seats() fails closed as described.
Verify that max_rounds defaults to 2 and is hard-capped at MAX_ROUNDS_CAP.
Check that per-call/council wall clock and prompt-token ceilings are enforced and produce budget_exhausted turns.
Verify that prior turns are re-read from the chain, not from in-memory reply.
Check that roles rotate between rounds.
Verify that evidence is never interpolated into role/instruction portion of prompt.
Check that every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn per round (content, refusal, unavailable, budget_exhausted).
Verify that degraded is set when fewer responded than requested.
Check that CouncilRecord.render prints degraded adjacent to findings.
Verify that the falsification protocol is not yet implemented but stated.
Check that CLI --live and --dry-run behave as described.
Verify that daedalus council command uses default_participants which builds real adapters.

claims.why: No implementation of round logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Prior turns are re-read FROM THE CHAIN, not from the in-memory reply
claims.why: No chain reading code in this chunk.

claims.why: No definition of max_rounds parameter or MAX_ROUNDS_CAP in this chunk.

claims.text: evidence is NEVER interpolated into the role/instruction portion of a prompt -- the role line is session-authored constant text, the PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE comes next, and only then does any untrusted byte appear, inside a fenced evidence block rendered by the ADAPTER (vendors.CouncilAdapter.assemble), which also enforces withholding.
claims.why: No prompt construction code in this chunk; references vendors.CouncilAdapter.assemble which is not present.

claims.text: Per-call wall clock, per-council wall clock, and a per-council prompt-token ceiling CHARGED BEFORE DISPATCH (transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); a per-call timeout does not bound token spend).  Blowing a budget produces a chained budget_exhausted turn and ends the council -- it never silently shortens a round.
claims.where: docstring 'HARD BOUNDS, ALL FAIL-CLOSED AND ALL RECORDED'
claims.why: No budget enforcement code in this chunk.

claims.text: A hung vendor is abandoned on a daemon thread at the per-call cap and recorded as unavailable/timeout; it can degrade the quorum, never block the session.
claims.where: docstring 'HARD BOUNDS, ALL FAIL-CLOSED AND ALL RECORDED'
claims.why: No threading or timeout code in this chunk.

claims.text: Every REQUESTED participant produces exactly one chained turn per round -- content, refusal, unavailable with a machine reason, or budget_exhausted.
claims.why: No turn production code in this chunk.

claims.text: requested/seated/responded and distinct_classes (independence is a property of WEIGHTS, not sockets) ride on the record, degraded is set whenever fewer responded than were requested, and CouncilRecord.render prints it ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS, not in a footer
claims.why: No CouncilRecord definition or render method in this chunk.

claims.text: convene takes live and it DEFAULTS TO FALSE.  Seating any adapter that still carries a SHIPPED transport -- the code that spawns claude, codex or ssh ... agy, or opens the Ollama socket -- raises LiveCouncilRefused before the roster is chained and before a single byte is dispatched.
claims.where: docstring 'LIVE WIRING IS OFF BY DEFAULT'
claims.why: No convene() implementation in this chunk.
